name: Baseline: codx-junior maintenance board is unplannable (363 tasks, no owners/priorities/dates)
description:
**First shift baseline (2026-11-16 19:25).** Findings from reading the board; the plan for the next shifts.

**State found**
1. `codx-junior maintenance` holds **363 tasks** across ad-hoc columns (`Harness`, `To Do`, `Backlog`, `Blocked`, `UI`) with **non-canonical statuses** and mostly **no priority, no assignee, no due date** — it cannot be forecast or demoed in this shape.
2. The columns are **not** delivery columns: 50+ cards sit in `Harness`, which mixes finished work, open questions and abandoned chats.
3. Two cards titled as emergencies were in fact **shipped** and were only closed this shift: `8f8710cf` (backend unresponsive — P0 deployed and measured) and `720a3e48` (repo broken — fix merged, 399 chats confirmed). A third-party reader would wrongly believe the product was on fire.
4. Two real residuals had **no card at all** and were created this shift: JWT/HMAC key length (security) and `check_projects` fan-out back-pressure (P1 performance). Chat storage was already correctly tracked as `e65e733e`.

**Objective of this task:**
1. **Column cleanup:** define delivery columns on `codx-junior maintenance` (`To Do` / `Doing` / `Blocked` / `Done`) and move every card out of `Harness` into the truthful one. Close cards whose own summary proves them shipped.
2. **Triage the backlog:** for each card decide keep / close / merge-into-another. Cards with no summary, no owner and no date and older than ~14 days are candidates for `rejected` (not silently archived — record the reason).
3. **Rank and publish a milestone view:** top 10 by user-visible impact, each with owner profile, priority and a demo-able vertical slice. No technical-layer milestones.
4. **Report:** one page with the increment table (milestone · deliverable · owner · date · deployable · demoable) on the desk board, so management can diff it shift to shift.

**Acceptance:** no card left in `Harness`; every open card has priority + owner profile; a milestone table exists with dates and demo flags; the board count drops to a defensible number with a written reason for every closure.

**Not is scope:** changing any code or repository file — this shift plans and re-orders the board only.

**Hand-over note from the PM shift of 2026-11-16 19:35 — evidence gathered after this card was written. Use it so you do not redo the discovery.**

1. **`Doing` already exists** on `codx-junior maintenance`. Columns are now: `Harness, API, UI, Done, On Hold, Rejected, To Do, Doing, Backlog, In progress, Blocked`. Do not create it again; decide which of them survive and merge the rest.
2. **Non-canonical statuses actually in use** (sampled from the board listing): `Harness`, `API`, `UI`, `ui`, `To Do`, `On Hold`, `Backlog`, `doing`, and the empty string `-`. The canonical set is only `todo / doing / onhold / done / rejected`. Cards freshly created by tools come out with status `""` unless it is passed explicitly — treat that as `todo`.
3. **Two contradictory cards to look at first, both lying in the same way:** `c8632422` "Neverending tasks" is in column `Blocked` with status `onhold` **and progress 100** while its own summary lists two still-open items (the `live_turn_ids()`/`is_stale()` cancel bug and the missing ceilings). Progress 100 + onhold is the pattern of a card that was auto-closed, not finished.
4. **Increment M1 already exists** as sprint `Run: M1 stability hardening` with two cards: `c6c33374` (JWT key, due 2026-11-18, `doing`, work order sent to `codx-junior`) and `a314fc9c` (fan-out back-pressure, due 2026-11-20, `todo`). Rank your top-10 **around** M1, do not re-plan it.
5. **A blocker you own:** `4a1cf260` — `create_task()` rejects the `wake_at` keyword (live traceback this shift, same family as the `estimation_cost` bug that killed `a9906517`, `242c730f`, `183031f3`). While it is open, scheduling a follow-up through the plain task tool fails silently-ish. **Workaround that works:** create the follow-up with the board tool (`project_manager action=create_task`), which accepts `wake_at` — that is how the M1 checkpoint `fc944c49` was scheduled for 2026-11-18.
6. **Do not force priorities you cannot justify.** Every open card needs a priority and an owner *profile*; where the card carries no evidence of urgency, set `low` and say so — a truthful `low` beats an invented `high`.

Scheduled follow-up: `fc944c49` (M1 checkpoint) wakes 2026-11-18 19:34 UTC, the same day this card is due. Keep the two consistent: if you re-date this card, note M1 in the same report.
